messages.author: c584965fac2b99d6
messages.subject: Problem with edits to global.R not being used
parts:
Hi

I've got a problem with a shiny project - http://glimmer.rstudio.com/psychemedia/nhssitrep/ - in which changes/edits I make to global.R are not being detected. ) can edit ui.R and server.R and the changes come in to effect. With global.R, it's as if a cached version of the file is being used.

If I copy the whole project directory to a new directory, the app runs fine. I tried restarting R but it doesn't seem to help?

tony

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Problem with edits to global.R not being used
parts:
It's a known limitation that a browser reload doesn't reload global.R, but just stopping runApp and re-running it should do it, much less restarting R. Yet you're the second person to report this.

- Can you try putting a print statement in global.R to see if its really not getting called at all unless you rename?
- Is there a stray .RData file, perhaps?

messages.subject: Re: Problem with edits to global.R not being used
parts: I have a json file that is used as a database, and it is read in global.R. The users are allowed to enter data through ui interface and save to (add to)  this json file. When I edited the json file from the server Linux box, the change is not reflected on the deployed Shiny web interface even after I clear the browser history. How/where are the old data obtained?
"stopping runApp and re-running it should do it"
does this mean this needs to be done by admin on the server?

messages.author: aacc6b267809c4ca
messages.subject: Re: Problem with edits to global.R not being used
parts: I am trying to separate data from the app, so the json file is saved in a separate dir different from the dir containing ui.R, server.R and global.R.  The app would read the json file, but if the Shiny app does not reload, this approach is not going to work. Any suggestions on solving the issue or different approach?

Hi Bob,

Try to create a file named "restart.txt" in your app directory and edit it each time you want to refresh the app.
Some documentation here : http://rstudio.github.io/shiny-server/latest/#restarting-an-application
